title_prefix: Any error raised by a message handler di
mechanism: safely-dispatch-peer-message (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1723-1738) wraps dispatch-ibd-message in (handler-case ... (error (c) ... (disconnect-peer peer))), so ANY condition of type ERROR raised anywhere below it -- a truncated payload, a bad count, or a bug of our own inside a handler -- disconnects the peer; drain-and-reap-peer repeats the same clause as its outer backstop (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1846-1854). Core does the opposite at the same point: ProcessMessages wraps ProcessMessage in try/catch and the handler is 'LogDebug(BCLog::NET, "%s(%s, %u bytes): Exception %s caught")' with the connection KEPT (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5269-5287: try at :5269, catch at :5283-5287); nothing in that catch calls Misbehaving or sets fDisconnect, so in Core punishment is only ever explicit, at a named rule inside a handler. PONG additionally has a hand-written forgiving branch: nAvail < sizeof(nonce) sets sProblem = "Short payload", cancels the outstanding ping, logs at debug and returns (:4990 for the handler, :5030-5035 for the branch that sets sProblem = "Short payload" and cancels the ping, :5043-5052 for the debug log). Our ping and pong handlers read the u64 unguarded through bl.bytes:with-byte-reader (src/networking/protocol.lisp:169-182), and the framing layer enforces only an UPPER bound on the payload (receive-message, src/networking/peer.lisp:624-629, +max-message-payload+) with no per-command minimum, so a 24-byte header declaring length 0 with the matching checksum reaches the handler and raises.
consequence: Verified with a positive control on five commands whose well-formed minimal payload IS accepted by the same fixture: ping, pong, feefilter, sendcmpct and notfound each raise SB-INT:INVALID-ARRAY-INDEX-ERROR on every shorter payload and each leaves the peer :DISCONNECTED, while a well-formed 8-byte pong leaves it :READY. Core keeps the connection for all five (pong by its named Short-payload branch; ping :4970-4973, feefilter :5123-5125, sendcmpct :3907-3910 and notfound :5150-5152 all deserialize unguarded and rely on the ProcessMessages catch). So a peer whose implementation has a benign framing quirk on any of these is dropped by us and forgiven by Core, and -- combined with the refill loop of 33c6687d -- is redialled within ~30 seconds to be dropped again, an endless connect/disconnect cycle we cause. The wider consequence is the one that makes this S2 rather than S3: the same clause converts ANY deserialization or logic bug in any of the 31 registered handlers into node-wide peer churn, because the failure is per-peer but the trigger is per-message-TYPE -- every peer that sends that message type is dropped, which is exactly the outcome Core's shape exists to prevent. It is not a cross-peer DoS: the peer dropped is always the sender, so an attacker can only disconnect itself.
evidence: Worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-p2p-s2, warm image, probe file ga11-probe/p2p.lisp. (a) The finder's five payloads reproduced through the shipped path: pong/0, pong/4, ping/0, feefilter/3, sendcmpct/1 -> handler raises SB-INT:INVALID-ARRAY-INDEX-ERROR, safely-dispatch-peer-message returns NIL, peer state :DISCONNECTED, in every case. (b) POSITIVE CONTROL: a well-formed 8-byte pong through the same call -> (:SURVIVED T :STATE :READY), so the disconnects are caused by the short payload and not by the fixture. (c) Controlled sweep over the handler table (31 registered handlers, bl.net::*p2p-handlers*), feeding each command its smallest WELL-FORMED payload first and only then shorter ones: exactly five commands accept their canonical payload and disconnect on every shorter one -- ping (canonical 8 B), pong (8 B), feefilter (8 B), sendcmpct (9 B), notfound (1 B). REFUTED as fixture artifacts, and therefore excluded from this verdict: addr, addrv2, getaddr, inv, getdata, headers, getheaders and getblocks all raise TYPE-ERROR on their canonical payload too, i.e. their errors come from the empty node-context (nil peers / address-book / chain-state), not from the short payload -- an uncontrolled first sweep listed them and they are not evidence. (d) Core read at refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:5269-5287 (the catch at :5283-5287: LogDebug only, no Misbehaving, no fDisconnect), :4990-5052 (PONG, with the Short payload branch at :5030-5035), :4970-4973 (PING), :5123-5133 (FEEFILTER), :3907-3921 (SENDCMPCT), :5150-5164 (NOTFOUND).
fix_shape: Give safely-dispatch-peer-message Core's shape: catch the handler's error, log it at debug with the command name and payload size (net_processing.cpp:5283-5287), and KEEP the connection, so a disconnect can only come from a named rule inside a handler -- the existing disconnect-peer / record-misbehavior call sites, which already carry Core's wording. Leave drain-and-reap-peer's stream-error / socket-condition / end-of-file clause exactly as it is: a dead socket is a different event, and Core reaps it in the transport. Framing-level failures (bad magic, oversized message, bad checksum) must also stay disconnects, since Core drops those in Transport::ReceivedBytes before ProcessMessage is reached. Then port Core's explicit pong branch (:5030-5035): fewer than 8 payload bytes cancels the outstanding ping, logs 'Short payload' at debug, and returns. Because forgiving every error also hides our own bugs -- which is the real cost of this change -- the swallowed condition needs a visible counter (a per-command failure count surfaced by getpeerinfo or the net log category, rate-limited) so a handler that starts throwing on every message is noticed instead of silently degrading. A regression test must send each of the five short payloads and assert the peer is still :READY afterwards, with the well-formed payload as the control.
